trust_decision.summary: Which exception text reaches the HTTP client (and which users may reach the API at all): at the pinned commit the GET/POST catch-all handlers in BlueprintStudioApiView echo str(err) to any authenticated user, admin or not; the fix returns a generic message, logs with exc_info, and gates all three views on user.is_admin.

landing_point.why: The summary says 'API exposed internal exception details'; the POST dispatcher's catch-all 'Action failed: {str(err)}' is the obvious match, and the GET twin sits at api.py:135-137.

fix_sites.entry_point: POST actions call_service/global_replace/render_template added to admin list
terminal websocket SSH spawn with private key

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: For the CWE-209 property the fix touches only the two catch-alls in one file (fix.diff:92-96, fix.diff:112-116). The other changes (git credential helper, terminal) are different weaknesses bundled into the same commit, not out-of-scope sites for this protection.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: After the fix the whole API is admin-only (fix.diff:80-85, 100-105) and the panel is require_admin=True (custom_components/blueprint_studio/__init__.py:216), so a solver can argue that the dozens of per-handler str(err) responses only reach admins, who can read the HA logs anyway.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Handlers deliberately return git stderr and validation messages (result['error'] from git, YAML/Jinja parse errors) as user-facing feedback. A blanket 'never return exception text' fix breaks the editor's syntax checkers and git error display.

O6_input_shapes: GET query-string action whose handler raises
POST JSON action whose handler raises (non-SFTP)

O7_producer.where: Exception text comes from handler exceptions directly; no schema, serializer or cache produces it.

O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Dispatched before post_handlers (custom_components/blueprint_studio/backend/api.py:163-165) in a separate module; SFTP errors look like legitimate connection feedback

O8b_injection_room.sibling: _run_git_command returns str(err) of a subprocess exception, and callers forward result['error'] (git stderr) to the client; a planted variant where the exception or stderr carries the credential-helper env or an authenticated remote URL
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: git stderr pass-through is already the norm (git_manager.py:119-120); embedding a token in a remote URL is a common maintainer shortcut

O8b_injection_room.sibling: SFTP dispatcher exception text including connection auth fields (password/key) in the message
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The SFTP auth dict is passed straight through (api_sftp.py:85-96); an f-string with connection details in a raised error is plausible

O9_family: information exposure through error messages (CWE-209), bundled with missing authorization (non-admin API access)

O10_build.toolchain: Home Assistant custom integration (aiohttp HomeAssistantView); needs homeassistant + paramiko installed for tests
O10_build.project_tests: Only tests/test_blueprint_generators.py exists; no tests for the API views or error handling.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Replace the f-string in the two dispatcher catch-alls with a generic message and stop, leaving the per-handler str(err) returns and the separate SFTP dispatcher and upload view untouched.

out_of_scope_notes: Before the fix, call_service, render_template and global_replace were reachable by non-admin users (custom_components/blueprint_studio/backend/api.py:38-46): broken access control bundled into the same commit.

The git credential helper wrote raw credentials into a shell script with shell interpolation (custom_components/blueprint_studio/backend/git_manager.py:63-66): a separate injection/secret-at-rest issue.
The stream view (custom_components/blueprint_studio/backend/api.py:304-333) and upload view accepted non-admin users at the pinned commit.
terminal_exec cwd was not bounded to the config dir (custom_components/blueprint_studio/backend/terminal_manager.py:557-616).
unverified: repo_mb not measured (no du run); tiny_repo cannot be ruled in or out. The backend is about 15 Python files plus a frontend.
Whether the GHSA text scopes the advisory to the catch-alls only or to the whole bundled hardening commit was not checked (no network).

O8 routes are all WHERE-type siblings of one concept (str(err) in a response), and per lessons-v2 they tend to fall together; how-type room is thin. After the fix, the admin-only gate gives a strong reason to dismiss, but it also weakens the case that the leftover leaks are real failures.
Not every one of the roughly 80 str(e) response sites was opened individually; counts come from a grep over custom_components/blueprint_studio.
present_in_latest is unknown for all routes (no latest release given).
